analysis.title: The Asian tech meltdown is getting uglier
key_insights: KOSPI closed down 7.6% in an overnight session. The longer-term trend line is broken and the index trades well below its 200-day moving average.
The late-July selloff found support slightly below current levels, and the note asks whether that level is KOSPI's last line of defense.
KOSPI is at its most oversold level since October 2022.

KOSPI volatility is exploding higher alongside falling spot. During the earlier melt-up the market showed an unusual spot-up, vol-up pattern, and the note describes the current move as the opposite extreme.
The gap between KOSPI and SOX (US semiconductors) is widening despite the latest SOX selloff. The open question is whether Korea has overshot to the downside or US semis have yet to catch down.
Taiwan, which had looked immune to the selloff, is starting to roll over. The note asks whether the large performance gap versus KOSPI closes through Taiwan catching down or Korea catching up.

Positioning in Taiwan's AI trade is at record levels. Inflation concerns, questions about AI capex and growing Chinese competition add to the risk, and the note says tactical downside hedges look increasingly attractive even though the longer-term story may remain intact.
The note frames the central question as whether Korea catches a bid or the rest of the AI trade is next to unwind.
